This placement maximises distance to the NEAREST victim instead. It also assumes 10% ribbon slack; see CONF-RIBBON-REACH, where the sensitivity is sharp. This does NOT resolve CONF-SINGLE-PICKUP-EMC; it improves the geometry the measurement will be taken on.

conflicts.field: how far the GPIO ribbon must travel between POD_PI and POD_HAT
sources: register: GPIO_RIBBON is a fixed 100.0 mm part
derived: edge-to-edge pocket clearance understates the run badly once the pockets sit diagonally - a layout with a 48.3 mm edge gap needs 118.8 mm of ribbon

derived: the Pi 5's 40-pin header runs along the long edge of the board and the HAT's mates with it, so each header sits at its pocket's x centre on one of the two x-aligned edges; the run is the best of those four pairings
derived: sweeping usable ribbon length gives POD_PI-to-pickup 74.1 mm at 100, 74.1 at 95, 71.6 at 90, 71.6 at 85, and 11.6 at 80
conflicts.ruling: HEADER-TO-HEADER SPAN GOVERNS, NOT EDGE CLEARANCE. This caught a real error: the first relocation was ruled on edge-to-edge clearance and produced a layout needing 118.8 mm of a 100 mm ribbon - not buildable. The corrected placement spans 89.9 mm, holding 10.1 mm of slack. THE SENSITIVITY IS A CLIFF, NOT A SLOPE: anything from 0 to 15% slack keeps the Pi 71-74 mm from the pickup, but at 20% the packing collapses back to the original 11.6 mm layout. 10% was chosen because zero slack allows no bend radius or connector entry and buys only 2.5 mm of extra clearance. IF A LONGER RIBBON IS SOURCED the constraint relaxes and the search should be re-run; nothing here depends on 100 mm being the only option.

conflicts.field: whether the battery pack should be placed as an aggressor alongside the Pi
sources: derived: the ruled layout leaves the pack 8.60 mm from the pickup coil and 10.00 mm from the analog board - closer to the coil than anything else in the instrument, and placed there only because it was fitted last, wherever it fit
derived: holding the Pi and HAT where CONF-POD-EMC-CLEARANCE puts them, the pack has EXACTLY ONE legal site in the whole body. 8.60 mm is not a choice, it is forced

derived: raising the required pack clearance to 12 mm collapses the Pi from 71.6 mm to 11.6 mm from the coil; every floor from 12 to 35 mm gives the same collapsed layout, and 40 mm does not pack at all

derived: ranking pack and Pi as EQUAL aggressors (maximise the worst of four pairs) reaches a worst case of 16.1 mm, but does it by moving the Pi to 17.9 mm from the coil - trading 54 mm of Pi clearance for 7 mm of pack clearance
conflicts.ruling: NO CHANGE TO THE LAYOUT. The re-solve was run and it VALIDATES the ruled placement rather than replacing it. THE CHOICE IS BINARY, NOT A CONTINUUM: the only real estate far from the coil is the upper bout the deleted neck pickup vacated, and exactly one pocket can occupy it. Either the Pi is far and the pack is close, or the reverse. There is no intermediate layout - the sweep from 12 to 35 mm returns the SAME collapsed result at every step. The Pi keeps the space because it is the dominant aggressor: a 2.4 GHz radio, multi-rail switching regulators and load-dependent current transients, against a pack that is quiet at DC and switches only through its protection and charging circuitry. THE PACK'S EXPOSURE IS REAL AND IS MITIGATED LOCALLY, not geometrically: twisted pack leads, a grounded shield can around the chamber, and charging electronics kept outside the pocket. Those are cheap; a Pi 11.6 mm from a single coil is not fixable at all. Record the pack as a SECONDARY aggressor in the EMC procedure so the measurement separates its contribution from the Pi's, rather than assuming it away.

conflicts.ruling: CANNOT BE SETTLED BY DERIVATION. This is the first question in the program that needs a physical measurement rather than a calculation. Procedure written at docs/geometry/SG_PICKUP_EMC_MOCKUP_PROCEDURE.md; no measurement has been taken. The comparison is against a conventional single-coil guitar's ambient floor, NOT against silence, and discrete switching tones are weighted above broadband hiss. GEOMETRY IMPROVED but the question stands: CONF-POD-EMC-CLEARANCE took the separation from 11.6 mm to 71.6 mm, close to the most this outline allows, and distance alone does not establish a pass. CONSEQUENCE IF IT FAILS: a hum-cancelling pickup changes the route dimensions, which re-opens the packing ruled in CONF-SINGLE-PICKUP-SPACE. Cavity shielding is now the leading mitigation, because the cheap geometric one has been spent.

provenance.note: Physical geometry only. Derived from the component register; stated spec dimensions are compared, never consumed.

notes: INTERNAL physical geometry record. Contains no cost, price, or manufacturing-time fields by design.

Every cavity dimension in the paired geometry record is DERIVED from this register. Nothing downstream reads a stated cavity dimension, which is why a stale note like 'total_height_mm: 76.0' cannot propagate.
stated_* fields exist only so the derivation can be compared against the source specs. They are never inputs.

The source scan behind this register was BOUNDED and is not exhaustive. It covered sg-spec, luthiers-toolbox instrument_geometry, and tap_tone_pi hardware docs. string_master_v.4.0 was not fully searched. Absence of a conflict record is not evidence that no conflict exists.

min_floor_mm is 8.0 on every cavity: an engineering estimate, not a structural calculation. The pod sits in the lower bout near the control cavity and the battery routing, so the real minimum should come from a structural review under string tension.
The derived pod footprint is a LOWER BOUND. The Hi-Z buffered splitter is required by the canonical signal chain and has no dimensions anywhere, so it could not be included.

This record derives cavity SIZE only. It does not validate cavity POSITION against the body outline, so it cannot detect two cavities colliding in plan or a cavity breaching the perimeter. Plan-level collision checking needs the traced outline and is out of scope. CONF-OPPOSED-FACE-WEB is a concrete instance of what that omission hides.

Pickups, pickup routes, the neck pocket, the bridge, the control cavity, and the output jack are NOT modelled here. This register covers the embedded-electronics cavities only: the pod, the Teensy pocket, and the battery chamber. Pickup disagreements are recorded as conflicts (CONF-PICKUP-TYPE, CONF-PICKUP-ROUTE-DIMS) but no pickup dimension is derived or fit-checked.

Because top-face routes are excluded, the derived body thickness is a LOWER BOUND in a second way: it accounts only for back-face cavity depth plus floor, never for a top-face route cutting toward the same plane from the other side.
